query: Which method can be used for oxidation resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Applying stationary friction processing (SFP) to AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys will improve their oxidation resistance by refining the grain structure, which in turn promotes the rapid formation of protective oxide layers (mainly Cr2O3 and Al2O3).
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast/coarse-grained AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy that typically forms nonprotective spinel oxides during oxidation.
generation.intervention: Subject the alloy to stationary friction processing at high rotational speeds (e.g., 1800 rpm for 5 minutes) to create an ultrafine-grain microstructure.
generation.conditions: Isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at elevated temperatures (e.g., 850–1050 °C) for extended durations (approximately 100 hours).
generation.structural_mediator: Ultrafine-grain microstructure with an increased density of grain boundaries.
generation.mechanism: The refined microstructure enhances the diffusion of Cr and Al along the abundant grain boundaries, facilitating the rapid formation of dense, protective Cr2O3 and Al2O3 layers. These layers are more effective at reducing further oxygen ingress compared to the nonprotective spinel oxides that form on as-cast samples.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to as-cast samples, SFP-processed alloys will exhibit lower cumulative mass gain and reduced oxidation kinetics (i.e., lower parabolic rate constants), with XRD/SEM analyses showing a predominance of protective oxide phases.
generation.baseline: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi alloy oxidized under similar conditions, forming nonprotective spinel oxides with higher mass gain and faster oxidation rates.
generation.boundary: The effectiveness of oxidation resistance may vary with processing parameters (rotational speed, duration) and the specific oxidation environment; optimal conditions might be alloy- and temperature-dependent.
generation.uncertainty: The precise quantitative improvement in oxidation kinetics and the relative contributions of Cr and Al diffusion require further experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy samples: one set in the as-cast condition and the other processed using SFP at 1800 rpm for 5 minutes. Expose both sets to isothermal oxidation in air at selected temperatures (e.g., 850 °C, 950 °C, and 1050 °C) for 100 hours. Monitor mass gain over time and perform XRD and SEM characterization of the oxide scales.
measurements: Oxide scale phase composition and morphology (via XRD/SEM)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the SFP-processed samples do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in cumulative mass gain or parabolic oxidation rate constants (e.g., <20% improvement) compared to the as-cast samples, or if the oxides formed are not predominantly protective (i.e., mainly Cr2O3 and Al2O3), then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: How does an ultrafine-grain microstructure, obtained via stationary friction processing, affect the oxidation behavior of AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy?. System: Equimolar AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy (HEA). Processing: Stationary friction processing (SFP) using a WC-cylindrical tool (12 mm diameter) at rotational speeds of 400 rpm and 1800 rpm for 5 min duration. Test conditions: Isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at 850, 950, and 1050 °C for 100 h. Findings: Grain size refined from 98 μm (as-cast) to 1 μm (SFP_400) and 0.43 μm (SFP_1800).; Phase transformation from BCC/B2 to FCC occurred, with 38% and 55% FCC fraction for SFP_400 and SFP_1800, respectively.; Surface free energy increased by 29.8% for SFP_400 and 35.2% for SFP_1800 compared to as-cast.; Oxidation kinetics decelerated by 12–20% for SFP_400 and 38–48% for SFP_1800 compared to as-cast.; Cumulative mass gain at 850 °C after 100 h was 0.33 mg/cm² (as-cast), 0.27 mg/cm² (SFP_400), and 0.17 mg/cm² (SFP_1800).; Parabolic rate constants (k_p) at 1050 °C were 23.2 × 10⁻¹³ g²·cm⁻⁴·s⁻¹ (as-cast), 18.4 × 10⁻¹³ (SFP_400), and 8.16 × 10⁻¹³ (SFP_1800).; Processed samples formed predominantly protective
